Then after having to reset the app because it decided to load for 10 more minutes while trying to get to the dashboard. It finally loaded the dashboard upon my third reset of the app, and what I saw was nothing. No spending breakdown or information despite it saying I linked my account, no hint that it had logged the information of my monthly income and just no information at all with a prompt that said “link your account”. On top of all that this app has the gall to ask you to pay for it after the free trial before you even have a chance to experience it. This app feels like a poorly put together cheap cash grab. I can hope that in the future it gets the updates it needs and is actually functional. But for now I think 0 stars is an understatement for how bad of an experience this app was. title: Great App "with exceptions"
body: I think that Caleb and his team have done a fantastic job with this app. It looks and works so much better than the original version I tried when it was still the Simpler Budget app. So why the one star? Simply, I cannot connect my Apple Card to this app, which is something I can do with the premium version of their competitor Monarch (which costs the same annually). This may not be a dealbreaker for some, but for my wife and I it is. We use our Apple Card basically as our debit card. Everything except out mortgage routes through it, and then we just pay it off once or twice a month, tracking all our expenses from there because it tracks it more accurately than my bank statements. That said, with it unable to connect to Dollarwise, the app just confuses it as debt payments, which isn't what it is. It makes the app impossible to track my budget on, and while I think the app itself is great, and I want to switch and support the Hammer team, this is a deal breaker for me. I hope to check back in another year as my Monarch annual renews, and find that integration added.

title: No Longer Functional or Personal
body: I’m so glad that so many people love the new update, but honestly it removed all functionality for me. I’m in the minority for sure but can’t be the only one that’s better off with a journal and planning spreadsheet. Maybe I’m just doing personal finance wrong but that doesn’t feel right. I really wanted this to work but it might not be right for me anymore. The “safe to spend” doesn’t seem accurate because you can’t manually enter future auto payments that will be coming out or estimate future income you’ll have coming in so that’s just not accounted for it seems. I was using that to see what had already been portioned out or “spent” and what was actually safe to spend daily, now I’m just not sure where that number comes from or includes. The unadjustable ten categories are NOT making personal finance more personal as often claimed, and some of them just dont cover everything I was tracking before, the custom categories were so much better. I’d much rather have the option to put in transactions manually than be forced to put in my banking details, even if that makes it more streamlined. I do like seeing that x% is going to needs/wants/savings, and I’m glad the 50/30/20 ratios can be adjusted, but it’s just extra information cluttering the top of the screen that I don’t need. I know I’m putting more than “recommended” towards needs there’s nothing to be done about that and it stresses me out seeing it.

title: Tried because of Caleb Hammer
body: I listen to a ton of financial audit while driving for work, with his baked in adds, it finally got to me to give it a shot. Let me say, I am very disappointed. Issues I have: 1. Extremely inflated income estimation that seems to come from nowhere, I made sure to go through and check all items labeled as income and yet it was calculating about 230% of my actual monthly income. 2. When sorting activity you can't click into the purchase to see what account it was from, when you have multiple accounts and some used solely by your partner or others, you don't always know what a charge is for, but if I could click to see what account, it would help me figure it out faster 3. No insights based on estimated income, in the pie chart section, I could put whatever I want in each section, so I could budget $1,000 for everything without it telling me that I'm over my monthly income that I manually put in. Should subtract from the income and show you how much you have left to distribute, and offer AI insights of where to put more money. 4. Too many options for categories, when Caleb does his budget he pretty much has housing, debt payments, TP fund, groceries, utilities/bills, fuel, and fun/misc money the app is preloaded with SOO many tags, it's so cumbersome and then your having to create your own and delete out others. 5. The app is not intuitive, I was searching Google trying to find instructions to use it and ended up finding someone's YouTube series just to get a basic understanding. Things you would think would be simple like on the home tab, it shows "income" and "fixed-spending" one would think you could click those to modify or view where it's coming from, but no such luck. 6. The insights are confusing and can be unhelpful, it's labeling my mortgage as an unusual purchase even though there's 2 years history and all are categorized yet still "unusual purchase" 7. When you are in the insights tab, and inside of each category, it gives you a bar graph of previous months. Can you click to the previous months to see transactions? No. Can you click the down arrow next to "this month" to see other months? No. This app has a LOT of potential! I love the auto syncing to the accounts, being able to connect my bank and credit and other all in one spot is awesome! But due to my experience I have actually canceled my subscription and I am not even out of the 3 day free trial yet. I am not saying I wouldn't come back but would need to see updates and fixes in order to do so. Between my experience and thinking about spending $100 a year on this app, I will go back and spend an hour on my spreadsheet to re-organize and use that. Love Financial Audit, just disappointed that the app is clunky, cumbersome, and overall not an enjoyable experience. I hope improvements are made at which point I will be back!

title: Dollar unwise
body: I’m a fan of Caleb’s show, and my wife and I (younger millennials) manage our finances well. We’re committed to improving our financial habits, so I decided to download the app. The app has undergone a design overhaul, and I appreciate the data it provides regarding spending, saving, and bills. However, it lacks guidance on how to effectively budget. Instead of offering detailed insights, it presents a pie chart and some bar charts, leaving us to figure out how to make improvements on our own. The app doesn’t provide live notifications like other financial apps, and the AI is not helpful or even present. Instead, we’re forced to sort our expenses using a confusing “wants, needs, spends” swiping feature, which takes up a lot of time. I don’t want to spend hours swiping when I paid for an app designed to assist me. Furthermore, there’s no option to customize your financial goals. We’re stuck with the default 50/30/20 plan, which is a good starting point, but I’d like more flexibility in setting our own targets. Overall, I’m disappointed with this app. I had high expectations based on Caleb’s hype, but it falls short of delivering on those promises. For now, I’ll continue using my spreadsheets and tracking my finances in a more traditional manner.

That was a big disappointment, but the real deal-breaker was that there didn’t seem to be a way to add goals to a category - for example I need to save up a certain amount by a certain date (ex. putting aside a set amount of money to buy a toddler bed that we’ll be purchasing at an unknown time). I want to make sure that money is accounted for but it doesn’t make sense to set up a monthly budget for it when I want it to end at a certain dollar value. I didn’t get far enough into the process of setting up categories to see if Dollarwise has a way to split a transaction between different categories, say between medications and groceries. I’m sure Dollarwise works great for people that are looking for a simpler, more streamlined experience, but it doesn’t have the flexibility or customization that I’m looking for in a budgeting app.

title: Missing major feature for me
body: It’s a solid app and honestly better for overall budgeting than what I’m currently using. That said, it falls short for daily tracking. I’m very visual and need to see a day-by-day dollar amount to stay on top of things. For the past 20 years, I’ve used calendar-based budgeting apps where I can set recurring transactions like paychecks and fixed expenses (mortgage, etc.), then layer in other spending. Everything ties out to my bank daily, so I can quickly see at a glance (with the daily balance on the actual calendar) whether I have room to pay extra toward a credit card or if I’m at risk of overdrafting. I’ll keep using this alongside my current app because it does some things really well, but it can’t fully replace a calendar-style system for me.

title: Too much friction
body: There’s still a bit of difficulty adding accounts. If you have a more standard account like capital one or chime, adding accounts are a breeze. But once you start getting into those niche (but supported) banks, you get lags. If you have a passkey for your bank, you have to turn it off, which I have no intent on doing. So, while it does seem to have some promise, not being able to add all of my accounts makes it a useless unless I only want to track my more frivolous spending. Will be canceling my free trial for now. Would also prefer more than 3 days to get a good feel of the app. I understand it might not be feasible at this moment to offer longer but it doesn’t feel feasible to know if it’s actually worth it within 3 days when most people only get paid biweekly. Even as someone who gets paid weekly, there’s different “phases” in the post paycheck period. To sum it up, solid progress from its start but still too much friction. I guess I expected more for such a short free trial period. But it’s laggy enough for me to decide to cancel it for now. Not even worth waiting the full 3 days.

title: Meh

title: Great
body: Love this app! I just wish it had a calendar feature to track upcoming bills and payments so I could manage everything more easily. It would also be awesome if you could cancel subscriptions directly through the app. Those features would make an already great app even better!

title: Caleb=🐐
body: I got this app because of Financial Audit. I like knowing that Caleb has been in the trenches of debt, and knows how it is. I thought I was good at budgeting through my notes app, but once I typed everything out, and saw how much I was actually spending, I was surprised. title: Great potential
body: I like it and enjoy it definitely fairly easy to navigate but still seems a little slow at adjusting when you make changes and can be kind of annoying

title: A good start to finances
body: I am a long time fan and downloaded the app roughly two weeks ago and connected my bank account and brokerage. I enjoy the simplicity of the app and sorting transactions by the three main categories (Want, Need, and Savings) as well as all of the subclasses you can assign for the transactions. That being said, I do wish the app use the aggregate information of the last 3 months to create a calendar that displays dates when automatically renewing purchases or subscriptions or pay day deposits are (similar to some other apps). I just think it would be a really good feature to implement in order to better track and project monthly budgets by knowing when all the bills come due by looking at a single calendar that’s already tied into the finances. Other than that, this app is a very good and simple way to track your spending and budgeting! - a less broke medical student

title: Good, but room for improvement
body: Premium user. It’s nice to see all accounts connected in one place. That said, I do find myself still checking my bank account somewhat regularly, as dollarwise’s figures appear to be based on the actual live balance (‘completed transactions’), not your balance accounting for posted and pending payments. This means a sometimes several hundred dollar difference between what my bank account shows as available to spend and what DollarWise suggests - meaning I could overspend if I’m not checking my actual checking account. Don’t use this app as-is for a daily check if you’re cutting it close on your checking account.

title: Wish List

There are a few things I wish it could do but honestly if it did I think it would make it more confusing to use so I think it’s just right the way it is.

title: Good overall

It does take a minute to figure out how it works and transfers between accounts flood the transaction reviews. Overall a great app and budget tool.

title: Doesn’t work for me
body: Seems like a nice app but as soon as I tried to sign up I realized there was no way to add my Apple Card. I’m able to do so with Monarch so I’ll be sticking with that. This app really only works for traditional bank accounts

title: Great w room for improvement!
body: I have been an avid watcher for almost 2 years. I finally am in a place I can comfortably afford this extra subscription. After playing around with it for a few hours, I can see the benefits and potential. A few suggestions: When we change a category, it would be helpful if we had the option to apply to all the transactions from the same merchant. I’m manually changing each category to ensure the budget is accurate. (All my mortgage payments showed as other instead of housing) I added my investment accounts to get a better picture of my overall financial situation and well now every dividend or share I buy is showing up in my budget. It would be nice to be able to exclude a certain account from the budget. Also. Would be nice to make one budget across the board instead of putting in the numbers monthly. It should be automated once I enter my budget for the year. Oh, and I cannot get my Amazon credit card to connected idk if it’s an issue with the website but that’s unfortunate. Otherwise, I do see how this will be helpful and I plan on keeping it. I look forward to future updates!!! Thanks Caleb Media Team. <3

title: Categories that made me laugh
body: So far the app is nice. You do have to go one by one and review every category of your purchase because it does not categorize well. Here are a few that made me laugh. Health: Sephora Bath and Body Works My Nails Anyways wish you could select Sephora and choose change all at least for the subject. Update: I’ve been using the app now for a little bit and it is pretty clean. The categories are still a little frustrating but what I wanted to add is, what do you use for your stock investments?? Like category? That’s the only transaction I can’t figure out because it keeps going under my spending, but it’s just my stocks automatically moving back-and-forth through my investment company. 😭

title: Nice revamp
body: I like the revamp, it’s nice! The app is intuitive and I like the swiping mechanism for reviewing transactions. It’s easy to read, simple budget buckets without having to name every single one! I’m rating it 4 stars, one star off because: The one thing that would be a great improvement for your next update would be removing accounts without a full bank account disconnect! For example, the app doesn’t differentiate between transactions coming from multiple accounts from one connected banking app. This makes the budget off, it would be nice to remove an account from the linked bank without fully disconnecting the whole thing.

title: Not a bad app
body: Spent a few hours getting everything all set up, and went thru it with my wife. The app is not bad. It syncs to all our accounts, bank, HYSA, investments, etc. and it gives a pretty good breakdown of spending and setting up budgets for the various categories. It does about everything we wanted. But, we found another app that has a little more flexibility with categories, ability to share with another user, is usable on the web, and still a competitive price.

title: Counts the same transactions multiple times after sorting
body: It is very nice and user friendly but some minor bugs that can be easily sorted out. There is potential just needs a bit more work to be perfect!

title: Wish it would update better
body: For some reason it been saying I’ve had 1 dollar in my account for two months even tho I had over 500 in there constantly and it say I get paid 800 a month when I make over 3k a month

title: Still Not Syncing
body: I like that you can categorize your own purchases. But I don’t like that it’s not syncing on its own. I have to sync it myself. Also, on the connected accounts side it says one number, but then on the main page accounts side it shows a different number. For example: $3400 on my connected checking account, but only $591 on the main page for that same account. It’s been stuck on that same $591 for 3 days.

title: UX… I wanted to love it more
body: I’ll be the first to say Im hard to please when it comes to budgeting apps. They’re overwhelming and confusing even though they’re supposed to simplify budgeting. This one was on track but it was EXHAUSTING to go through each transaction to make sure it was categorized appropriately and figure out how much I allocate where and what each function means. And I wasn’t able to connect 1 account so I feel like I’m budgeting with one eye closed. I know this app is new and it will improve with time and support. So I felt like leaving a review with my feedback.

title: Great app - needs a few minor things
body: The new app is miles better then the old one. UI and design is the best I have seen in a budget app. The only reason for the 4 star is because they do not allow splitting transactions so if I go somewhere like Walmart and get different things like groceries and dog stuff, I am unable to add that to multiple categories. Also they do not support every card (Apple card not supported) and without that it make it hard to know everything happening in you finances.

title: Disappointing update
body: I was super excited for the update and overall love the UI. However the ability to use custom categories is essential to me. I wish there was a way to toggle that on or off or something. I can see how the lack of customization will work better for some, but it won’t for me. I canceled my sub.

title: Makes managing money a lot easier
body: The old version was super clunky and not intuitive at all. I like that the new version leaves room for personalization while still wrangling my spending habits.

title: It’s Good But Could Be Better
body: I’ve enjoyed Financial Audit so I got the app in Jan. Worked really well minus transactions duplicating but I could delete them. The update in Feb deleted my budget and now I can’t change the categories to get them back into my budget. I like it but it could be better.

title: Update/ beta
body: Liking the new app but can you make it so we can see what we’re typing in when filling in a budget and also when suggesting a category? The keyboard covers it up.

title: Almost perfect
body: Overall the app is extremely helpful. Once I connected my account it gave an immediate reality check of what my bills really were. I like I can create my own categories but if I try to edit a transaction to put it in the proper place it doesn’t move. Says it’s been updated but nothing happens. And every transaction at a gas station is considered “fuel” again can’t fix it or move it. Also 2+ day lag on transaction updates. Took 3 days for my direct deposit to show up. I tried the 3 day free trial and would like to change my subscription to monthly but no way to do it.

title: Registration and Subscription Issues

I am still awaiting support to contact me, but this has been a little frustrating.

title: Amazing!!
body: At first I just wanted to do the feel trial, and of course accidentally forgot to cancel. But thank goodness I didn’t. This is been the best budgeting app I have used so far. Easy to understand and set timelines for payoffs. Definitely would pick this over the others, just upset I didn’t use the promotional code to get the free signed cookbook. Also a big fan of the show!

title: Bank options
body: I came to the review page to ask this question because I couldn’t pull up support on the website but I was wondering if at all probable you guys can get it to allow Cash App as a connecting bank me and many others that I know use Cash App and I think it would open up to even more people if we could use it

title: Thank you Dollarwise!
body: I got this app because of watching Financial Audit, and I have to say it really put my money use in a clear and easy to understand way! I was genuinely shocked to see how much money I was wasting and it helped me take a deeper look at where my money was going. I’m going to be fully honest, I ended up deleting 16 subscriptions, 7 of which I didn’t even know I had and it was a huge relief. Love this app, totally recommend it!

title: Use it
body: Great app that is growing on the active feedback from its users.

title: Caleb would hate my spending
body: Just got the app so can save and manage my money correctly. Overall its a good app, maybe missing like more ways on how to save up or ideas and set like a good plan but im glad it just shows the different categories and money. I hope with every few updates or checking out with app I’ll be in better position than I’m in now.

title: Amazing
body: I knew I had an issue with money, especially since I recently found financial audit and started watching it a lot. This app made me see how absolutely horrible I am at managing my money. I buy little things here and there, not thinking it could have that much of an impact. But seeing this app lay it out all in one space makes me feel like a financial idiot- likely rightfully so. I hope using it, and sticking to it, will help me budget successfully.

title: Still New To It
body: But I love how easily the app condenses and categorizes all my spending. Love how the format is simple, too. So excited to use it more.

title: WARNING
body: I downloaded this app (a recommendation from financial audit) but completely forgot all about it. I never registered for an account, meaning they should not have access to any of my contact or billing information. Somehow, about a few days later, my card was charged $14.99 from “dollarwise.com” although I never made a purchase with them, much less start a subscription. Keep that in mind if you still continue to use this app! You will always need to keep your cards locked and thankfully I do that regardless so they couldn’t take $15 out of my account!

title: Download
body: Out the door download was easy. I plugged in my checking account. From the get go everything is smooth going. The only thing I couldn't do is pay for it. It does have a 3 day free trial right as of today and that's good. I'll consider paying for it one day. I was laid off late Aug. Had been looking for a job since Dec when we heard about it. Finally found a job yay me! But I won't get a paycheck till Oct 9. The pricing is not bad. It's just not doable right now. Every person should consider getting this. My debt is bad and I want to get it under control. Try it!

title: Awesome
body: I really like the app, I wish it had a feature where you could add your kids and they could only access there portal but as a parent we can access both our own and the kids portal but they could watch and track there spending/savings and as a parent we could help them give advice and teach them good habits from young ages.

title: Excellent customer service
body: I had a few small issues logging into my device. The Dollarwise team responded immediately, on a holiday weekend, to resolve the issue. The team solved my issue and I was able to resume budgeting better!! Great app with great support.

title: Love it.
body: I learned about this app through Financial audit, I love you it lets you itemized the purchases from “ needs and wants” I saved over $700 Last month just by learning about my small purchases that were adding up.

title: Awesome sauce
body: Great app. Very easy to link bank info, and see where I can improve.

title: Works with all my accounts really well
body: Works great with all my accounts I have multiple brokerages with Robinhood and it tracks my trades really well which helps given rh has a pretty bad p&l system

title: great app
body: I used the built in finance tracker that my bank had and it didn’t work nearly as well. Dollarwise is so organized and took away all the clunkiness I was fed up with from using other services. Just streamlined and easy to use

title: Finally
body: It’s nice to see a budgeting app actually correctly tracks everything in an organized and easy to understand way.

title: I was crashing out like a toddler
body: This app is good and does as advertised. In a world of content creator slop, Caleb Hammer delivers on this product. (But still a little heavy handed on the ads)

title: Budgeting at its FINEST!!!
body: This app has helped me to understand my budget and spending habits! I’ve been able to start a savings account and change my habits within the first 2 months. I’ve tried Rocket money and it SUCKED compared to this one!!! Thank you Dollarwise!!!

title: Eye opening!
body: I watch the YouTube videos with my partner, I see people who are in far worse positions, succeeding at getting on the right track, this showed me I can get where I want to be with discipline and drive! Dollar wise made it 100 times easier to see my own habits and what I need to work on. Thank you to the dollar wise developers for making this journey possible!

title: Love it!
body: Between this and financial audit I feel like big changes are to come in my future!

title: PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE
body: Please get this app!! I thought I was great with budgeting and knew where my money was going. I was wrong! I didn’t realize how much “little things” I bought had such a huge impact on a monthly bases! Every Walmart, gas station and sweet treat cost me over 1,000 a month that could have been put into my savings account. This app helped my husband and I take accountability and realize how irresponsible we have been with our money. Please get this app! It is worth the money. Helped us open our eyes on our true spending habits. It gave us the exact tools we needed to plan a reasonable budget. Helped us plan for our future and pay off our debt even quicker!!!!

title: Great App
body: Great financial tracking on spending. Use it everyday to save money and pay debt.

title: Great budgeting app
body: I’ve used several budgeting apps and since updating this app it is definitely the best budgeting app I’ve ever used.

title: Totally Improved App with A + Support
body: For those who have used the previous DollarWise: this is majorly improved. Especially with the custom categories Everything works the way you’d expect it to. I’ve tried rocket money in the past and it is so so clunky compared to this. title: Give it time
body: The free trial feels like getting your feet wet before jumping into the deep end of the financial world. Coming from Monarch, I wasn’t sure what to expect, so I kept both apps for a while to see if one stood out more than the other. I also compared Credit Karma and Experian alongside Monarch to see how each one handled categorizing transactions and how easy they were to read during a daily or every-other-day money check-in. Setup was a little difficult with both, and tracking felt harder at first. I wanted to give each app enough time so I could look back and really compare which one worked better for me. After a couple of weeks, DollarWise started to click. The Insights page made it much easier to clearly see where my money was going. To be fair, we were also in the middle of selling and buying a home, so our inflow and outflow were dramatically higher over the last three months. Because of that, the “unusual spending” alerts kept showing up on my home screen. I’m hoping that settles down soon. To make a long story short, DollarWise is easy to read and does a good job categorizing spending with clear graphs that show where your money is going. So far, I’m preferring it over the other options I’ve tried.

title: Great app for tracking expenses
body: After the revamp last month, I’ve been really liking the app. It’s easy to use and lets me see an easy to understand summary of my expenses. Suggestions for future updates, I’d like to see the ability to assign Categories within the Review Transactions area, as not all transactions are assigned the category they should be/I want them in. Right now it’s an extra step to assign categories. I’d also like to see a Back functionality added to when you are viewing transactions of a specific type. It’s annoying to be looking at a specific months’ transactions, want to see how often I am spending at a specific vendor and then need to redo all of the menu navigation to get back to where I was. For context I’m talking about this path: Insights > specific category > this month > click on specific transaction to see all transactions to that vendor. There should be a back arrow or something to bring me back to the ‘this month’ or ‘category’ screen.
